Pixels or Features

The 17 flowers of the notebook, described two ways: by the pixels of a 32 × 32 thumbnail (3,072 numbers), or by the 512 numbers a pretrained ResNet-18 computes before its last layer. Pick a test photo and compare its nearest training photos in both spaces, then look at the whole training set projected onto two dimensions with PCA. Nothing is trained on the flowers here: the features come straight from ImageNet.

One test photo of each kind; the first is the buttercup of the slides.

k-nearest neighbors, Lecture 12: a test photo gets the most common label among its k nearest training photos (a tie goes to the class of the nearest one).

PCA of the training photos

Each dot is one of the 680 training photos, placed by the first two principal components of its vector (Lecture 11). The ring is the test photo. Two dimensions keep only part of the story: the k-NN accuracy uses all 3,072 or all 512 numbers.

the same comparison in Python (the notebook's variables) 

    

  






  

    
Pixels see color and layout
Two photos are close in pixel space when the same colors sit in the same places. A yellow buttercup in the middle of the frame is close to a yellow dandelion in the middle of the frame, and far from a buttercup photographed from the side.

    
Features see the flower
The 512 numbers each say how strongly one learned pattern (a petal shape, a texture, a center) is present anywhere in the photo. Photos of the same kind of flower end up close even when color, position and background differ.
